 "answer": "The evidence supports transformed visual correspondence, but complete matching segment boundaries remain unverified [E29][E33].

Reported matching sample times are A 5.900 s ↔ B 11.000 s, A 6.900 s ↔ B 12.000 s, A 11.100 s ↔ B 16.200 s, and A 12.100 s ↔ B 17.200 s [E54][E50][E55][E51][E56][E52][E57][E53]. These samples suggest an offset of approximately +5.1 seconds in B, without establishing continuous correspondence between the samples [E54][E50][E57][E53].

The alignment reports a candidate range of A 13.314–19.133 s ↔ B 18.354–24.225 s; its endpoints are not verified correspondence boundaries [E29][E33]. A also has black upper and lower borders and different watermark placement [E11][E37]. These scene similarities support transformed correspondence, not exact synchronization of those two particular frames [E11][E37].

A complete interval mapping, including the remaining portions of both videos, was not established; unmatched intervals should not be interpreted as confirmed absence of correspondence [E29]. Content correspondence does not establish original authorship [E29][E33]. Audio was not assessed; the media profiles report zero audio tracks in both inputs [E3][E12]."

{
 "decision": "FINISH",
 "answer": "Both videos show a yellow-shirted cyclist on a red bicycle, but the available evidence does not authenticate B as the original source [E4][E26][E12]. At 0.72 seconds, the cyclist’s position, bicycle framing and background differ across the two images [E23]. Equal-time comparison detects pixel differences from 0.04 to 4.04 seconds, with the endpoint excluded; this does not establish corresponding moments because temporal alignment found no matches [E25][E21].

A lasts 10.2 seconds and B lasts 4.04 seconds, making A 6.16 seconds longer [E3][E12]. A’s sampled images at 3.84, 6.32 and 8.92 seconds show changing pedalling positions, so those observations do not support calling A a single frozen image throughout [E7][E31][E11]. The unmatched A interval from 4.04 to 10.2 seconds is additional viewing time, but it is not evidence that B omitted a particular event [E25]. Continuous action and correspondence throughout that interval remain unverified by the sampled images [E31][E11][E21].

A has no audio track; B has one, so their available sound presentation differs [E3][E12]. B’s speech analysis returned no transcript, which does not establish silence; spoken content, music, other sounds and their effect on interpretation remain unverified [E34].

The confirmed differences affect viewing duration, the motion shown at equal playback times and audio availability [E3][E12][E23]. They do not establish a different underlying event, an editing method or which version was altered; the temporal relationship remains unresolved [E21][E25]."
}
